attempted_claim: Let C be the middle-third Cantor set in [0,1] with IFS f0(x)=x/3, f1(x)=x/3+2/3, let mu be its unique logarithmic equilibrium probability measure, and let I00,I01,I10,I11 be the four closed level-2 cylinders from left to right. By reflection symmetry mu(I00)=mu(I11) and mu(I01)=mu(I10). Prove or disprove that |mu(I00)-1/4|>=0.005, i.e. that the equilibrium mass of an extreme level-2 cylinder differs from the uniform self-similar value 1/4 by at least 0.005. A complete answer is a rigorous proof of this separation for mu, or a rigorous proof that |mu(I00)-1/4|<0.005 (hence uniformity within the stated tolerance), with all error terms certified.
claim_type: quantitative non-uniformity of equilibrium mass on cylinders
decisive_failure: No certified statement about the equilibrium measure mu is established: the numerical value ~0.287 is an uncertified finite-section limit, the energy-gap, minorant-loss, and relaxation-shortfall figures are float-guided pilots backed by interval widths only for the upper competitor (2.5e-5), and the structural dust-concentration diagnosis is a feasibility assessment rather than a proved impossibility theorem. All scripts and partial interval machinery are preserved in output/artifacts/ for reproducibility, but nothing here meets the target's all-errors-certified standard.
